topics.title: Object Oriented Programming
topics.content: Java is a statically typed, object-oriented programming language. The main object-oriented principles are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

topics.title: Collections
topics.content: The Java Collections Framework provides interfaces and implementations such as List, Set, Map, ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet, TreeSet, HashMap, LinkedHashMap, and TreeMap.

topics.title: HashMap
topics.content: HashMap stores key-value pairs and provides average constant-time complexity for get and put operations when hash distribution is good. HashMap allows one null key and multiple null values.

topics.title: Exception Handling
topics.content: Java exception handling uses try, catch, finally, throw, and throws. Checked exceptions are checked at compile time, while unchecked exceptions generally extend RuntimeException.

topics.title: ExecutorService
topics.content: ExecutorService provides thread-pool management and is generally preferred over manually creating many threads.

topics.title: Synchronization
topics.content: The synchronized keyword provides mutual exclusion and establishes memory visibility guarantees between threads.

topics.title: Volatile
topics.content: A volatile variable guarantees visibility of writes between threads but does not make compound operations such as increment atomic.

topics.title: CompletableFuture
topics.content: CompletableFuture supports asynchronous programming and can compose multiple asynchronous operations using thenApply, thenCompose, thenCombine, exceptionally, and handle.

topics.title: Streams
topics.content: Java Streams provide a declarative way to process collections. Common operations include filter, map, flatMap, sorted, distinct, collect, reduce, and groupingBy.

topics.title: Generics
topics.content: Generics provide compile-time type safety and reduce the need for explicit casts. Wildcards include ?, ? extends T, and ? super T.

topics.title: Reflection
topics.content: Reflection allows Java programs to inspect classes, methods, fields, constructors, and annotations at runtime.

topics.title: JVM
topics.content: The Java Virtual Machine executes Java bytecode. Important JVM areas include the heap, stack, metaspace, program counter, and native method stack.

topics.title: Dependency Injection
topics.content: Dependency injection allows objects to receive their dependencies rather than constructing them directly. Constructor injection is generally preferred because dependencies can be final and required dependencies are explicit.

topics.title: REST APIs
topics.content: Spring Boot provides annotations such as RestController, GetMapping, PostMapping, PutMapping, and DeleteMapping for building REST APIs.

topics.title: Configuration
topics.content: Spring Boot configuration can be provided using application.properties or application.yml.

topics.title: RAG
topics.content: A typical RAG pipeline contains document ingestion, document reading, transformation, embedding generation, vector storage, retrieval, and prompt augmentation.

topics.title: Document
topics.content: Spring AI provides abstractions such as Document, DocumentReader, DocumentTransformer, VectorStore, EmbeddingModel, and ChatModel.

topics.title: TokenTextSplitter
topics.content: TokenTextSplitter can divide large documents into smaller chunks before embedding. Chunk size should be selected according to the embedding model, document structure, and retrieval requirements.

topics.title: Vector Store
topics.content: A RAG system retrieves relevant document chunks from a vector store and provides them as context to an LLM before generating the final answer.
